Usually, yes. Tired from a short night or a long workday is a different thing from run down, and a lot of good sessions start with a flat warm-up. My rule is to start the warm-up and see how the first couple of working sets feel. If the bar speed is there, carry on. If it's a grind, cut the volume, drop a set or two, and leave a few reps in the tank rather than chasing numbers.

If you're tired day after day, sleep, food and total workload are the first places I'd look. I can build you a lighter session for today if you want one.
